justification: Perspective whose contribution is a conceptual framework of three interaction regimes, team composition and communication protocols for agent societies; it argues and structures the field, offering no evaluation.

Contribution is one-shot generation of the communication topology and interaction modes of a multi-agent system; evidence is author-run experiments reporting token and accuracy gains over state-of-the-art methods.

Contribution is deterministic EMA-guided routing that picks which agents answer and merges them; evidence is accuracy and cost comparisons on discrete-choice benchmarks against single-model and ensemble baselines, all in-lab.
Contribution is continuous reallocation of subtasks across agents in an activity-on-vertex workflow graph; evidence is author-run empirical comparisons on practical tasks, not use in a real setting.
Contribution is a PSO-style outer loop that generates and iteratively refines the agent system itself from feedback; evidence is lab benchmark gains such as +261.8% over ADAS on TravelPlanner.

Contribution is RAPS, a publish-subscribe messaging substrate with reactive subscription and Bayesian reputation to isolate peers, i.e. the arrangement itself; evidence is lab experiments over five benchmarks.

Contribution is inference-time adaptation of the communication topology, agent roles, links and execution order; evidence is benchmark scores on five suites against single- and multi-agent baselines in the lab.

Contribution is a response-conditioned DAG built from Shapley-style peer assessment that regulates message propagation, i.e. the interaction structure; evidence is lab experiments with strong and weak backends.

Contribution is an evolutionary outer loop (feedback-conditioned mutation and crossover over configurations plus experience memory) that rewrites the agent system between runs; evidence is lab results on BBEH, SWE-Bench and WorkBench.

Contribution is an agentic optimizer using interaction trajectories and task feedback as loss signals to evolve the MAS over long horizons; evidence is accuracy on four agentic benchmarks with three backbones, lab only.

Contribution is decentralized coordination: parallel agents claim subtasks from a queue and communicate through a shared verified context instead of a central controller; evidence is SWE-bench Verified and LongBench-v2 lab runs.

Contribution is structuring a multi-agent system under an explicit cost budget via ILP model selection and RL topology choice, claiming up to 86% cost reduction; evidence is lab comparison on three representative tasks.

Contribution compares multi-agent structures (single agent, subagent, agent team) under fixed compute-time budgets and issues design guidelines; the comparison runs in a controlled testbed, not in production.

Vision paper proposing NOMA, an optimization loop over pipeline topology, model and engine choices across agents, argued with one controlled experiment on a 10-agent pipeline rather than a full validation.

Contribution is transactional plan control: a versioned execution log with restore points and localized repair that edits only the affected region of the plan; evidence is job-shop benchmarks (DMU, TA) run in the lab.

Contribution is a graph-theoretic account of consensus in signed, directed agent interaction networks and topology restrictions that stabilize it; evidence is theorems plus lab ensembles of LLaMA-3, Mistral and Gemma agents.

Contribution is a trainable policy that predicts a sparse communication DAG switching a team between parallel and sequential modes; evidence is lab runs varying agent count, task and underlying agent.

Contribution treats coordination configuration as a separable architectural layer, comparing five configurations with model, tools and prompt held fixed; evidence is a controlled 100-market study, the live deployment still accumulating.

Contribution is an auction-based economy that decides which agent acts and how credit is assigned, i.e. decentralized coordination without a central orchestrator; evidence is lab results on five agentic tasks against monolithic baselines.

Contribution is a per-agent communication hub that selects sparse partners and generates dense message transformations, i.e. the inter-agent channel itself; evidence is lab benchmark comparisons with dense-communication baselines.
Contribution is MASS, a staged search that rewrites agent prompts and then topologies from evaluation feedback; evidence is lab comparisons against a spectrum of existing multi-agent alternatives.

Contribution is a runtime uncertainty-management lifecycle (representation, identification, evolution, adaptation) governing whether the system may proceed; it is only demonstrated for feasibility on one clinical system.

Contribution is an LLM orchestrator that incrementally plans and adapts a workflow encoded as a Datalog+/- program fixing which tool call runs next; evidence is author-run financial use cases, not deployed practice.

Contribution is targeted recovery after diagnosis, mapping observed failure signals to repair actions and comparing against retry-only and full replanning; evidence is a lab fault-injection study with a budget sweep.

Contribution is an instrument for studying loop failure: AgentFail, 307 real failure cases from two production orchestration platforms, with root-cause and repair-difficulty analysis of workflows running in practice.
